split_policy.sealed_test_rule: Do not open until metric code, training protocol, checkpoint selection and thresholds are frozen.

units.rendered_depth: metres internally, absolute and signed residuals reported in millimetres

coordinates.MHR_wrapper: raw MHR vertices in metres, multiply coordinates by [1,-1,-1], then add pred_cam_t
coordinates.heldout_transform: Camera-A MHR -> world using A inverse extrinsic -> Camera-B using B world-to-camera extrinsic
coordinates.renderer_conversion: pyrender camera pose diag(1,-1,-1,1) maps OpenGL camera to the OpenCV camera frame
coordinates.pixel_projection: u=fx*x/z+cx, v=fy*y/z+cy; nearest pixel centre for depth comparison

legacy.definition: one-sided Camera-B observed point to nearest MHR vertex
legacy.known_bias: penalizes points over triangle interiors according to mesh vertex density

point_to_triangle.definition: one-sided Camera-B observed point to closest point on any MHR triangle
point_to_triangle.implementation: exact triangle-region distance; conservative centroid bounding-sphere tree only prunes triangles whose lower bound cannot win

rendered_depth.definition: absolute Camera-B observed Z minus rasterized MHR Z at overlapping held-out color pixels
rendered_depth.visibility: GPU depth buffer keeps the front-most MHR surface; explicit two-sided triangles prevent EGL backface-driver differences
rendered_depth.zero_depth: no rendered overlap and excluded from residual distribution

surface_training_gradient_contract.loss: robust observed point to differentiable barycentric triangle-surface samples
surface_training_gradient_contract.chain: loss -> triangle samples -> MHR vertices and pred_cam_t -> raw pose/camera outputs -> head_pose.proj and head_camera.proj
surface_training_gradient_contract.audit_only: gradient audit executes zero optimizer steps and writes no checkpoint

claim_limits: HuMMan person masks describe clothed/person surface, not bare-back skin.
One-sided point-to-triangle does not penalize unobserved mesh regions.
Rendered-depth residual is reported only with overlap coverage.
DEV5 selects implementation choices; it is not a sealed generalization result.
